headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad API/browser egress plus Airbyte’s data-pipeline role creates default data-leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte can ingest external data through its API/data-pipeline role, and RD-Agent can run browsers and call external APIs, so a content-to-instructions bridge is plausible if outputs are copied into workflows. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven; uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Airbyte-ingested content is later pasted into RD-Agent prompts or browser tasks
IF an operator uses a shared workspace or clipboard bridge between the two agents
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of raw pipeline outputs into prompts
Add a manual review step before any browser task uses Airbyte-derived text
Separate workspaces for ingestion artifacts and agent prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; RD-Agent handles financial reports, research papers, logs, and secrets, and also calls third-party APIs. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive material can flow from either agent to external services by default, creating exfiltration risk.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem or mounted workspace
IF RD-Agent is configured with live API keys while processing Airbyte outputs
IF Airbyte pipelines include sensitive business data
mitigations: Use separate workspaces and credentials for each agent
Rotate or scope API keys before running RD-Agent
Restrict Airbyte jobs to non-sensitive datasets
Review outbound destinations for both agents before execution
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and secret redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and RD-Agent supports multiple instances. Airbyte writes via its API-driven integration workflows, so concurrent mutation of shared external resources is plausible even without explicit filesystem write fields. The exact overlap is not fully documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same downstream API, database, or dataset
IF RD-Agent runs multiple instances against the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign disjoint datasets or API targets
Serialize jobs that touch the same resource
Use per-agent credentials with least privilege
Check for duplicate writes in logs after each run
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent is a research/automation agent that can act on outputs and uses browsers/APIs, while Airbyte produces data-pipeline outputs. If RD-Agent treats Airbyte-derived data as authoritative, errors can cascade into external actions or reports. Because the pair lacks documented verification boundaries, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes Airbyte outputs without an explicit verification step
IF downstream browser/API actions are triggered from those outputs
mitigations: Require human approval before any action based on Airbyte data
Add source-validation checks in RD-Agent prompts
Compare Airbyte outputs against a second source for critical fields
Log and diff all transformed records before publication
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware gating

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte handles business data, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and secrets and sends data to third-party APIs. That combination can create retention, residency, or contractual mismatches, but the profiles do not document a specific jurisdictional violation, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated or contractual data is routed through RD-Agent APIs
IF retention policies differ between Airbyte storage and RD-Agent logs
mitigations: Classify datasets before routing them to either agent
Exclude regulated data from RD-Agent runs
Set short log retention and verify deletion behavior
Confirm vendor terms for each external API used
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
